raw:
{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging" },
  "read": "The students who skipped the reading are now sitting through a discussion where everyone can see they have nothing to offer. That is a public competence threat — they look checked out or unprepared in front of their peers — and it is quietly eroding the sense that they belong in this intellectual space. The students who did the reading feel used, which is a status wound of its own: their effort is propping up people who opted out.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Call out the unpreparedness in the moment — 'Clearly some of you didn't do the reading' — which shames publicly and shuts down the exact participation you want, while turning the prepared students into informants against their classmates." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the standard that everyone comes prepared and everyone contributes, while giving the unprepared students a low-stakes on-ramp right now so they can re-enter the discussion with something real to say, not just sit there burning.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The reading is required and the discussion depends on it — that does not change.",
    "Every student is expected to contribute something substantive, not just nod along."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Let unprepared students take two silent minutes right now to skim a key passage or prompt before the discussion resumes.",
    "Allow contributions that are questions or connections, not just recall — so students who read partially can still enter honestly.",
    "Vary how preparation is checked going forward: a quick written response at the door, a turn-and-talk at the start, a one-sentence stake-your-claim — so it is not always the same students visibly carrying things."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Okay, pause for a second. I am noticing the energy in here and I want to be straight with you about what I am seeing, because I think you can handle that." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Here is the thing: some of you came in loaded for this conversation and some of you did not, and that gap is real. I am not going to pretend it is not there. What I want to know is — if you are sitting here without much to work with, what would actually help you get into this right now, in the next two minutes?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what we are going to do. I am giving everyone two minutes. If you read it, use that time to pick the one moment in the text that would change this conversation if we talked about it. If you did not, flip to page — and skim the first two paragraphs. Find one question it raises for you. That is your entry point. Two minutes, then we go." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I want to be clear about something before we restart. I hold you to this because the reading is how we think together — it is not a hoop. And I genuinely believe every person in this room is capable of showing up prepared. So going forward, that is the expectation. Today we reset; tomorrow we come in ready. I am holding that bar because I know you can clear it." }
  ],
  "longGame": "After class, check in briefly with the students who were visibly carrying the discussion — name that their preparation mattered and that you noticed — and separately create a low-key structure for the next reading cycle, like a quick entry ticket, that makes preparation a habit before the public pressure of discussion, so the divide does not keep recreating itself."
}
situation: Half the class did the reading and half clearly did not, and the half that did is getting visibly annoyed at carrying discussions.
